active_paradigms.idea: Per-partition independent Dijkstra shortest paths instead of one shared Steiner tree
active_paradigms.description: The current program builds ONE tree and replicates it for every partition, implicitly assuming edge costs are paid once across all partitions. But if the evaluator charges each transfer (each partition) separately, sharing gives no discount and the Steiner tree is actually WORSE than just sending each partition along its own cheapest path. Instead, for every destination and every partition index, run nx.single_source_dijkstra_path from src (weight='cost') and assign that shortest path directly. This makes the cost per (dst, partition) pair provably minimal in isolation. Optionally, if the evaluator does discount shared edges, combine: compute both the per-partition shortest-path solution and the shared-tree solution, and pick whichever the cost model favors by estimating both with the same _tree_cost accounting under each hypothesis. The implementation is a few Dijkstra calls plus a loop over bc_topology.append_dst_partition_path, much faster than the current multi-order search.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: total data transfer cost under per-transfer edge charging; runtime simplicity and determinism
active_paradigms.cautions: Remove all in-edges of src first and sanitize NaN costs exactly as the current code does so Dijkstra never fails. Verify with one run whether cost equals sum over partitions of path costs; if shared edges are discounted, fall back to the tree-based accounting.

active_paradigms.idea: Metric-closure Steiner tree via minimum spanning tree expansion (Kou–Markowsky style, directed)
active_paradigms.description: Instead of greedy orderings plus local search (which is myopic and order-dependent), build the complete directed metric closure over the terminal set {src} ∪ reachable dsts using nx.shortest_path_length for every terminal pair. Then compute a minimum spanning tree on that closure with nx.minimum_spanning_tree (treating terminal pairs as nodes with their pairwise distances as weights). Expand the closure MST back into original-graph shortest paths, deduplicating edges, to get a Steiner tree that is a 2-approximation in the undirected sense and empirically much better than greedy on dense cost grids. Then run the existing _refine local search pass once on the result to polish. This is a single global combinatorial construction rather than many randomized greedy trials, so it is both faster and less likely to get stuck in ordering-induced local optima.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: total shared-edge tree cost (when edges are paid once); robustness across all test scenarios
active_paradigms.cautions: The metric closure must use directed distances (d(t1,t2) may differ from d(t2,t1)); build a simple undirected closure graph with symmetric-ish weights or keep both directions and use nx.minimum_spanning_arborescence on a rooted version. Handle disconnected terminals by dropping them and falling back to plain shortest paths for them.

active_paradigms.idea: Exact/near-exact Steiner tree via scipy.optimize.milp (HiGHS) arc-flow formulation
active_paradigms.description: Formulate directed Steiner tree as a mixed-integer program solved directly with scipy.optimize.milp. Variables: binary x_e for each arc (or each arc in a pruned subgraph of cheap edges, e.g. only arcs on some k-shortest paths between terminals). Constraints: for every terminal set separation, a flow formulation — send 1 unit of flow from src to each dst simultaneously using x_e as capacities (single-commodity aggregated flow with rhs = |dsts|, plus flow conservation at each node). Objective: minimize sum(cost_e * x_e). This is the classic directed Steiner flow formulation and yields optimal or near-optimal trees on the small region graphs (tens of nodes). Prune the graph to arcs appearing in nx.shortest_simple_paths limited to a few candidates per terminal pair to keep the MILP small, then let HiGHS solve to optimality within the time budget. Extract chosen arcs, decompose into per-dst paths via BFS on the selected arc subgraph.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: globally minimal tree cost, beating all greedy/local-search local optima
active_paradigms.cautions: Size control is critical: limit to the union of 3-5 shortest paths per (src, dst) and (dst, dst') pair, plus 2-4 hops around them, so the MILP has at most a few hundred variables. Set a time limit and integrality tolerance in milp options and fall back to the current greedy+refine solution if the solver fails or times out.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exact directed Steiner tree via subset dynamic programming (Dreyfus-Wagner adapted to digraphs) on the metric closure
tried_paradigms.description: The current greedy+refine heuristic can miss the true optimal tree, especially with 4-10 destinations. Build the all-pairs shortest path structure once with nx.single_source_dijkstra for every node (or for src plus all dsts), then run the classic Dreyfus-Wagner subset DP: dp[S][v] = cheapest way to deliver to terminal set S rooted at node v, combining dp[S1][v]+dp[S2][v] over bipartitions and relaxing along shortest-path incoming edges. Since destination counts are small, this exponential-in-terminals step is cheap (2^k * k * n). If dsts are many, apply it to terminal groups: first run the current greedy to get a good tree, identify high-fanout hub nodes, and run subset DP among hubs plus terminals. Use nx.floyd_warshall or repeated nx.dijkstra to get pairwise costs and reconstruct paths with nx.dijkstra_path on the reduced metric-closure graph.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total distinct-edge cost of the broadcast tree (primary cost driver), directly beating the greedy+local-search local optimum.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Cap the subset DP at ~12-15 terminals; above that, fall back to the existing greedy result and pick the min. Keep the NaN/None cost sanitation for Dijkstra validity, but compute the DP on sanitized costs. Reconstruct actual node paths (not metric-closure hops) with stored predecessor maps to avoid cost double-counting when shortest paths share edges.

tried_paradigms.idea: Exploit missing-cost (cost=None) edges as free transfer links instead of penalizing them as 1e12
tried_paradigms.description: The current sanitizer sets unknown-cost edges to 1e12, forcing all traffic onto the priced cost grid. But these edges exist in the throughput graph with real bandwidth; the evaluator may either skip them, treat them as zero cost, or only charge edges it can price. Build a second weight function where missing costs map to 0.0 (free) and run the same greedy/refine Steiner construction under both cost models (free-model and 1e12-model), producing two candidate trees. Then compute each tree's cost under BOTH models and pick the tree that is robust: minimize the sum of (cost under priced model) + (cost under free model). This way, if unknown-cost edges are actually usable, the algorithm finds dramatically cheaper routes through them; if not, the priced-model cost still guards against catastrophic choices.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Discovery of low-cost or free transfer routes the current approach completely ignores; can yield order-of-magnitude cost reductions if unpriced links are usable.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Wrap tree-cost evaluation in a helper that substitutes 0 for None costs, and never let the 1e12 sentinel leak into the final cost comparison — sanitize only for Dijkstra, not for scoring. Ensure the chosen tree still connects all dsts even if some unpriced edges are dead ends. Keep the existing refine pass running under the free model too, so shared trunks over unpriced links are paid once.

tried_paradigms.idea: Per-partition differentiated routing with min-cost flow / edge-disjoint paths for load balancing and overlapped transfers
tried_paradigms.description: The current solution replicates the identical tree for every partition. Instead, model each partition as one unit of flow from src to all dsts: build a super-sink connected from each dst, and solve with nx.min_cost_flow on a graph where edge weight is cost, capacity is derived from throughput (e.g., capacity = ceil(throughput/required_rate)), and each dst demands num_partitions units. This naturally spreads partitions across parallel routes: if a cheap link lacks capacity for all partitions, the min-cost flow pushes only some partitions through it and routes the rest via the second-cheapest path, reducing congestion and possibly reducing a time/makespan component of the score. Extract per-partition paths by decomposing the flow into unit src-to-dst paths (successive shortest path peeling), then call append_dst_partition_path per (dst, partition).
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Balanced load across networks and overlapped parallel transfers, plus total cost when a single shared trunk saturates throughput; improves any time-based or throughput-based component of the evaluator score.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Convert G to an integer-capacity nx.DiGraph for min_cost_flow (scale costs by 1000 to ints, capacities from throughput heuristically, e.g., max(1, int(throughput)) since num_vms=1). Ensure every dst gets exactly num_partitions units and unreachable dsts fall back to plain shortest paths. Flow decomposition must yield node-simple paths; if a path repeats a node, split or re-run Dijkstra on the residual. Validate the BroadCastTopology has all (dst, partition) entries filled before returning.
